```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h1.csv")

h1Data$Sex <- factor(h1Data$Sex,
                           levels=c("Men","Women","Prefer not to say"))
h2Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h2.csv")
```

## Hypothesis 1

Women will score higher on intensity of love compared to men.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Gender (`Sex`):** A categorical variable with three groups: Men, Women, and Prefer not to say
- **Intesnity of Love (`Love_how_much_1`):** Points allocated to intesnity of love from a total budget of 100 points. Higher values indicate greater love intensity.

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1Data$Sex)

# Summarize love intesity points separately for each group.
by(h1Data$Love_how_much_1, h1Data$Sex, summary)
```

### Graph

@fig-attractiveness shows the distribution of points by sex at birth. The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarizes the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-attractiveness
#| fig-cap: "Love Intesitiy, by Gender."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h1Data, aes(x = Sex, y = Love_how_much_1,
                   fill = Sex)) +
  geom_rain(alpha = 0.5, point.args = list(alpha = 0.04, size = 0.6, na.rm = T)) +
  labs(x = "Gender", y = "Love Intesnity") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


## H2. Confidence in finding a new partner and commitment

Overall romantic love will positively correlate with relationship duration.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Relationship Length (`Relationship_length`):** A single item asking how long their current relatioship is in years.
- **Overall Romantic Love (`all_love_score`):** The mean of available responses to `Love_1–15`. Each item ranges from 1 (Not at all) to 5 (Extremely); higher scores indicate greater overall love



```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2Data[, c("Relationship_length", "all_love_score")])

```

### Graph

@fig-commitment shows the relationship between realtionship length and overall love. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-commitment
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between relationship length and overall love."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = Relationship_length,
                   y = all_love_score)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = .04,
              alpha = .04, size = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Relationship Length",
       y = "Overall Love (1–5)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2Data$Relationship_length, h2Data$all_love_score, use = "complete.obs")
round(r, 2)
```

The correlation was `r round(r, 2)`, indicating a weak negative association.
